decisions.reason: BASE preserves Mungyeong’s evasive assurance that Jin will find out naturally.
SOL naturally captures the interruption and the polite “저기요” address.
SOL correctly renders “저기요?” as a puzzled “Excuse you?” rather than “Wait?”
SOL preserves the gaze alternating between Mungyeong and the sleeve-hidden short sword in natural English.
SOL keeps the deadpan directional excuse while making the spoken line more idiomatic.
BASE preserves the intended contrast with what Mungyeong was trying to say; “about to say” shifts it toward immediate timing.
SOL makes the implied direction explicit without changing the speaker’s teasing intent.
BASE retains the deliberate act of confirming that Mungyeong’s back had disappeared from sight.
SOL is the natural English idiom for the source’s “one mountain after another” complaint and keeps the punch.
BASE preserves the source’s visual image of his eyes going dark at the thought of the hardships ahead.
“Any real information” naturally conveys that the Quest contains no actionable information.
SOL preserves the quest’s meaning and all system fields while smoothing the explanatory prose.
“Looked over” is a natural rendering of repeatedly inspecting the Quest window.
SOL avoids redundant repetition while retaining the clear antecedent that an easy test would be strange.
SOL preserves the conditional, the one-per-generation transmission, and Jin’s current strength and position.
SOL naturally expresses the continuing train of thought leading to Jeok Cheongang’s face appearing.
SOL accurately renders the source’s lack of a formally established Master-Disciple relationship.
“Turned the words over” is a natural recast of privately fingering or dwelling on those titles.
The omitted noun in “tenderhearted” is recoverable and the characterization is unchanged.
SOL preserves the deliberately damp, affectionate image in a more vivid conversational form.
“Started walking” is a natural equivalent of beginning to move.
“Complacent” implies smug self-satisfaction, while the source means a carefree or comfortable assumption.
BASE preserves the joke that he would fabricate facts that never happened, not merely claim to have seen nothing.
“Searched everywhere” naturally conveys wandering from place to place in search of Jeok Cheongang.
BASE preserves the glossary-bound rendering of 노야 as “Old Master.”
BASE retains the explicit condition of finding the Master’s location rather than simply finding the Master.
“Continued making the rounds” naturally captures visiting multiple places after paying Gung Gibang.
“Fissure” remains a faithful narrow opening in the formation while fitting the supernatural context naturally.
SOL preserves the interrupted objection and makes the conversational “그런데 왜” flow naturally.
“Martial robe” is a natural setting-appropriate rendering of the garment being offered for signing.
The added phrase preserves the green-onion punchline while making the sentence idiomatic.
The source says 약 반 시진, approximately half a shichen or one hour; BASE has the wrong quantity.
“Walking around and talking” more precisely reflects 돌아다니며 while preserving the exhaustion.
SOL explicitly preserves the concession that Murim has not yet suffered environmental pollution.
BASE retains the established capitalized System term “Status” in the status-condition warning.
SOL preserves Jin’s fixation on the System window despite his body becoming paralyzed, in smoother syntax.
BASE preserves the repeated “naturally” that makes Mungyeong’s earlier statement deliberately evasive.
SOL normalizes the source ellipsis to the project’s English punctuation convention without changing the reaction.
SOL keeps the source’s backward-surging-blood image while delivering it in brisker narration.
“Blood carrying the paralysis powder” is a natural equivalent of the bloodstream carrying it and preserves the causal action.
“At once” naturally preserves the simultaneous appearance of the ring.
SOL uses the glossary-bound “Inventory” and naturally renders the ring scattering a strange sheen as gleaming.
SOL correctly uses the glossary-bound “divine artifact” for 신물.
SOL makes clear that Jin’s Scorching Yang Qi joins the conflict, preserving the source’s causal mechanism.
BASE preserves the established capitalized System term “Status” in the recovery notice.
SOL naturally depicts him releasing the breath he had been holding while muttering the curse.
“Set a trap” is the idiomatic English equivalent of laying the midnight trap.
The past perfect is grammatically appropriate for Jin’s initial belief before the later realization.
BASE preserves the physical action of the sudden attack making his legs go weak, which SOL reduces to a static condition.
